messages:
Alex Chen: Quick follow-up from today's arch sync — I sketched a 'release_gamut' concept for rollout metadata. It bundles a compact compatibility_vector, a stability_score, and a fallback_priority metric. Goal: give the router succinct signals instead of many ad-hoc pin fields. Thoughts?
Maria Gomez: Short — what's the exact shape? Can you paste an example?
Alex Chen: Sure, rough sketch:
```json
{
  "canonical_id": "model-bert-2026-01",
  "release_gamut": [
    {"variant": "bert-quant-a", "compat": ["ctx-4096", "ops-v2"], "stability": 0.92, "fallback_score": 10},
    {"variant": "bert-8bit-b", "compat": ["ctx-2048"], "stability": 0.78, "fallback_score": 30}
  ],
  "epoch": 202603,
  "lease_token": "lt_abc123"
}
```
Samir Patel: I like compactness. Two questions: 1) how does this affect hard client pins (dedicated)? 2) does fallback_score combine with cost?
Jin Park: Implementation note — keep canonical_id for hard pins. release_gamut should be advisory for smart routing. Also include epoch + lease_token so ops can revoke/rotate without breaking clients.
Priya Reddy: Telemetry ask: we need per-gamut eval buckets (small prompt sets) so we can detect regressions per-variant. Suggest adding an optional "eval_shards" label array.
Maria Gomez: Also need deterministic fallback precedence documented — teams will ask whether cost can override stability. We should make comparator explicit.
Alex Chen: Proposed comparator (deterministic): 1) hard pin / canonical_id binding, 2) release_gamut stability score (higher wins), 3) historical latency penalty (runtime metric), 4) cost weight (lower cost preferred), 5) tie-breaker by variant hash. This keeps stability first but lets cost matter when stability similar.
Samir Patel: Edge-case: tenant aliasing. If tenant sets an alias that maps multiple canonical_ids, does gamut apply to each?
Jin Park: Behavior proposal: resolve alias -> set of canonical_ids, compute best variant per-canonical using release_gamut, then pick canonical with highest resulting stability score. If tie, prefer lower cost. That keeps tenant override semantics while using gamut.
Priya Reddy: Ops migration plan to propose: (a) extend manifests to accept optional release_gamut (backwards compatible), (b) runtimes without support fall back to legacy pin behavior, (c) staged rollout with canary + eval_shard telemetry TTL = 72h before full switch.
deploy-bot: deploy: rollout-manifest-v3 applied to staging at 3390012350 :rocket:
Alex Chen: Thanks all — I'll draft a short RFC with the spec, comparator pseudo-code, and the migration plan. @Priya can you add concrete eval_shard examples? @Samir let's sync on tenant alias mapping details tomorrow.
Maria Gomez: :thumbsup:
